description: Second spike branch spike/fz-contract-obligations commit 761f2d46b settled the model after rereading northstar.html. Protocol domains are markers, not source provenance and not an up-front implementer set. The real fix should replace contract-side source-ref enforcement with resolved contract obligation classification: after resolve_spec_decl produces params/result/constraints, classify protocol-domain marker tags contained in the resolved arrow Ty plus bounds, store that obligation set on each ContractArrow, and derive structural enforceability from obligations.is_empty() until protocol-domain validation exists. Keep collect_spec_refs only for source_publish dependency/wait recording. Do not enumerate protocol implementations. Acceptance: direct protocol-domain specs carry obligations; mixed protocol-domain/concrete overload still emits spec/violation for concrete calls rejected by all enforceable arrows; protocol-domain markers in when-bounds are detected; plain alias expansion such as @type enum_int :: Enumerable.t(integer) carries the marker through TypeDef; spec_violation and spec_mixed_protocol_concrete_violation fail with spec/violation on run/interp/build; spec_ok and representative protocol/extern/runtime paths stay clean; cargo test --lib and clippy pass. Audit of 761f2d46b passed with nits: production should decide whether obligation identity remains BTreeSet<String> marker tags or becomes a typed protocol-domain key, and FunctionContract::from_resolved should not remain a footgun that silently creates enforceable arrows without obligations.
title: Classify protocol-domain contract obligations from resolved Ty, not source rewalks
